statements.t: Within these markets, we support critical facilities and projects—ranging from energy production, manufacturing, and utility grids to commercial buildings, data centers, geospatial services, civil infrastructure, environmental services, and public-sector operations at the federal, state, and local levels.

We may experience increased costs associated with the recent developments around tariffs between the United States, Canada, and other international jurisdictions and will continue to monitor market conditions and respond accordingly.
Although we look to mitigate the impact of these pressures with a combination of cost management and price initiatives, there can be no guarantee that these initiatives will be successful.
Revenue is recognized to depict the transfer of goods or services to a customer at an amount that reflects the consideration we expect to receive in exchange for those goods or services.
In addition, we will use available cash, borrowing capacity, and cash flows from operations to fund our operating leases, finance leases, debt repayments, and various other obligations as they arise.

The changes in our working capital that contributed to decreased cash flows from operations were primarily a result of increases in accounts receivable of $121.6 million and increases in contract assets of $13.6 million due to timing of project billing cycles, partially offset by increases in accrued expenses and other current liabilities of $55.9 million due to timing of payments.
